title: Cupsogue
summary: Cupsogue is a coastal placename on Great South Beach opposite Eastport, with related recorded forms including Cupsage and Cupsawege.
address_label: Cupsogue Beach / Great South Beach opposite Eastport, Town of Southampton, NY
history_content: Cupsogue is identified as a locality on the Great South Beach opposite Eastport. Later historical work notes that Cupsawege appears as a known reference point in late eighteenth-century land transactions, placing the name within the coastal and shore-whaling landscape of eastern Long Island.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Cupsage, Cupsogue, and Cupsawege. The surviving source text available for this place does not provide a secure translation, so the meaning remains uncertain.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous people around the world have been naming their spaces, as indeed all peoples have, since time immemorial.”

— Lynn Peplinski, Place Names (2018), Indigenous Peoples Atlas of Canada, opening paragraph
land_loss_content: Cupsogue keeps an Indigenous coastal placename visible in a landscape often described through later beach, park, and real-estate names. The name connects the present barrier beach with older Indigenous language, travel, fishing, and shore-use histories.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker places this locality on the Great South Beach opposite Eastport, broadly corresponding to the modern Cupsogue Beach area. Its exact historic extent remains uncertain.
